02 / Problem MOVESCAN

The survey is the bottleneck.

Every quote for a full‑service move starts with someone driving out to walk the house with a clipboard. It is slow, it has to be scheduled, and it caps how many leads a mover can quote in a week.

Customers wait days for a number. Movers lose the ones who booked with whoever answered first.

Today's survey
1 visit
Per estimate · scheduled · in person

03 / Demo — capture MOVESCAN

Phone‑first, and calm about it.

The customer starts a scan with no account and no card. Each room asks the two things a mover needs on site — stairs, elevator, long carry — then takes a few wide photos.

Loading copy narrates the real work: "Checking for duplicates across your photos."

04 / Demo — what it doesn't know MOVESCAN

It tells you what it's
not sure about — first.

Every AI demo this year says "the model sees a photo and names things." Judges have seen it. The interesting part is the other direction.

  • Low‑confidence items surface at the top, with the confidence % and the model's own stated reason.
  • "Partly hidden behind the sofa." "Only visible from one angle." — the model says why, in plain words.
  • One tap re‑checks a single item against the catalogue.
04 / 13 Demo
05 / Why it's trustworthy MOVESCAN

A range, not a
fake‑precise number.

  • The customer sees a range. It widens when the inventory is uncertain — computeTolerance adds a band for every low‑confidence or user‑added item.
  • A human specialist narrows it to a firm price. It never jumps to a different number — nothing reads as bait‑and‑switch.
  • The console reports inventory accuracy as a measured figure: the share of AI items a human accepted unchanged. An observation, not a claim.
05 / 13 Trust
06 / Cross‑frame de‑duplication MOVESCAN

Three photos of one sofa
is one sofa.

All of a room's photos go into a single Gemini call, so the model can reason about object identity across frames instead of counting each photo separately.

Each item carries seenInImages, so the review and the dispatcher both show the evidence: "seen in photos 1 and 2 · counted once."

06 / 13 De‑dup
07 / Not an estimate — a plan MOVESCAN

The inventory becomes
a moving plan.

Truck class, crew size, hours, packing materials and special‑handling flags are all derived from the inventory — deterministically, in lib/moving-plan.ts, with no extra AI calls.

Pure functions. Unit tested. "20ft box truck · 3 movers · 11 hours" is arithmetic, not a guess.

08 / The dispatcher side MOVESCAN

A different user, so a different console.

The customer flow is light and spacious. The dispatcher works a queue under time pressure — so it's a dark ops console: urgency rails, handling chips, mono ticket rows, and an accuracy hero computed from real edits.

09 / 13 Architecture
10 / Engineering choices MOVESCAN

Judgement, not just features.

The model classifies, the code computes
pricing.ts, moving-plan.ts, catalogue.ts, chart.ts import no network, no DB, no process.env — so every arithmetic step is unit‑tested without spending API quota.
A model cascade that cannot throw
Classifies the error first: malformed JSON → retry the same model; a 429 → escalate to a model with its own quota bucket; both fail → checked‑in fixtures behind a banner. Never an error page.
Authorization in the app layer, on purpose
Every query uses the service key, which bypasses RLS by design. session-access.ts guards the customer routes; "not yours" and "not found" both return 404 — a 403 would confirm the id exists.
Rate limiting is one atomic Postgres function
consume_quota locks every bucket row before checking, then spends from all of them or none — concurrent scans can't both take the last unit. Per‑device, per‑IP, per‑account.

12 / What we're not claiming MOVESCAN

Honest about the edges.

  • Recognition accuracy on real photos is not formally measured. The console's "accepted unchanged" figure is computed from seeded demo data — a demonstration of the mechanism, not a validated model claim.
  • Regulated estimates. US interstate moves fall under FMCSA rules (49 CFR 375). Agent review is the compliance control; a real price needs legal review first.
  • Photo PII. Interior photos catch faces and documents. Currently demo‑grade: private bucket, signed 1‑hour URLs. Production needs retention limits and deletion‑on‑request.
  • One rate card. Real movers price per cu ft, per lb, hourly or from tariff tables. A general pricing engine is its own project.
  • Currency. Pricing is hard‑coded USD; localisation is pending.
  • Travel fare from pickup/destination distance isn't built yet — see next slide.
12 / 13 Limits
13 / What's next MOVESCAN

Travel fare, by map pin.

The next feature adds distance‑based travel cost from pickup and destination. The spec calls for a map pin‑drop, not typed addresses — street addresses don't resolve reliably in Pakistan, where this is aimed.

That reasoning — design for where the users actually are — is the point.
